content_payload.back_text: A — a letter we will sound out today

slides.teacher_cue: Hold up the card. Ask: Do you know this letter? Good. Today we learn what SOUND it makes.
slides.expected_response: Students recognise the letter name. They do not need to know the sound yet.
slides.correction_move: Simply confirm the letter name and move on. Sound teaching comes in Block 03.

content_payload.back_text: S — a letter we will sound out today

slides.teacher_cue: Hold up the card. Ask: Do you know this letter? Good. Today we learn what SOUND it makes.
slides.expected_response: Students recognise the letter name. Sound teaching comes in Block 03.
slides.correction_move: Confirm the letter name and move on.

content_payload.back_text: T — a letter we will sound out today

slides.teacher_cue: Hold up the card. Ask: Do you know this letter? Today we learn the SOUND.
slides.expected_response: Students recognise the letter name.
slides.correction_move: Confirm and move on. Do not teach the sound here.

content_payload.prompt_text: Listen. Point to the letter you hear.
content_payload.reveal_text: The sound is /s/ — the letter S.

slides.teacher_cue: Say the sound /s/ clearly. Students point to their S card or S on the board.
slides.expected_response: Students identify S when they hear /s/.
slides.correction_move: Say /s/ again slowly. Show the S card. Repeat together.

slides.teacher_cue: New sound today. Watch my mouth. /s/ — like air from a snake. Your turn.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /s/ clearly — continuous airflow, no voicing.
slides.correction_move: Feel the air on your hand — /s/ keeps going. Contrast with /z/ (voiced). Repeat /s/ x3.

slides.teacher_cue: Second sound. Watch my mouth open wide. /a/ — short, open, quick. Your turn.
slides.expected_response: Students produce short /a/ — not /ɑː/ (father) and not /eɪ/ (name). Mouth open, quick stop.
slides.correction_move: Put hand under chin — jaw drops for /a/. Contrast with /eɪ/: 'a-a-a' not 'ay'. Repeat x3.

slides.teacher_cue: Third sound. Tongue tip up behind top teeth. /t/ — quick tap, no voice. Your turn.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /t/ as a clean, voiceless stop. No vowel addition after.
slides.correction_move: Say /t/ not /tuh/. Tap the table once — that quick. Repeat x3.

content_payload.korean_flag: Short /a/ does not exist in Korean. Students default to /ɑː/ or /eɪ/.
content_payload.correction_routine: Drop the jaw fully. Say 'cat' — the a is very short. Place hand under chin and feel the jaw open. Contrast with 'cake' — the ay slides up. Repeat 'cat — cake — cat' slowly.

slides.teacher_cue: Listen and point. Which sound did you hear — A or B? Play each and let students choose.
slides.expected_response: Students correctly identify short /a/ vs long /eɪ/.
slides.correction_move: Re-play both. Model the jaw drop for /a/. Repeat the discrimination x2.

content_payload.back_text: sat — to sit down and stay

slides.teacher_cue: Say this word after me: sat. Sat means to sit. Mime sitting. Say it together.
slides.expected_response: Students say 'sat' clearly. They connect it to the action of sitting.
slides.correction_move: Model again: sat. Three sounds — /s/ /a/ /t/. Say slowly then at speed.

content_payload.back_text: tap — a light hit or knock

slides.teacher_cue: Say this word after me: tap. Tap means to knock lightly. Tap your desk. Say together: tap.
slides.expected_response: Students say 'tap' and connect it to the physical gesture.
slides.correction_move: Model: tap. Three sounds — /t/ /a/ /p/. Tap desk as you say it.

content_payload.back_text: at — a position word (at school, at home)

slides.teacher_cue: Say this word: at. It tells us WHERE — at school, at home. Say together: at.
slides.expected_response: Students say 'at' clearly. Short vowel /a/ must be clean.
slides.correction_move: Model: at. Two sounds — /a/ /t/. Watch the jaw drop for /a/.

slides.teacher_cue: Let's build sat together. Which letter makes /s/? Drag it. Which letter makes /a/? Which makes /t/?
slides.expected_response: Students drag s → a → t in order. They say each sound as they place each letter.
slides.correction_move: Return to individual sounds. Say /s/ — show S card. Repeat. Then rebuild.

slides.teacher_cue: Now build tap. Which letter makes /t/? Then /a/? Then /p/? Say each sound as you place it.
slides.expected_response: Students build t → a → p correctly, voicing each phoneme as they go.
slides.correction_move: Isolate the tricky sound. Go back to the individual phoneme card and repeat. Then rebuild.

slides.teacher_cue: Now read these words aloud. Point to each word and say it clearly.
slides.expected_response: Students read all three words accurately without prompting. Short /a/ is clean in each.
slides.correction_move: Point to the vowel in the word. Say /a/ — jaw drop. Then blend: /s/ /a/ /t/. Read again.

slides.teacher_cue: Drag the words to build the sentence. Read it aloud when done: Sam sat.
slides.expected_response: Students build Sam → sat → . and read the full sentence fluently.
slides.correction_move: Read word by word first: Sam. Sat. Then together: Sam sat. Repeat x2.

slides.teacher_cue: Read both sentences. Point to each word. Say each sentence clearly.
slides.expected_response: Students read both sentences accurately with one-to-one word tracking.
slides.correction_move: Return to word-level reading. Read each word alone, then re-read the sentence.

content_payload.text_content:
Sam sat.
Sam sat at a tap.
Tap, tap.
Sam sat.
content_payload.comprehension_prompt: Read slowly and carefully. Point to each word.

slides.teacher_cue: Point to the first line. Read together. Then students read alone.
slides.expected_response: Students read the passage accurately. Every word is fully decoded.
slides.correction_move: Pause at the error word. Point to each letter. Blend again: /s/ /a/ /m/. Re-read the line.

content_payload.text_content:
Sam sat.
Sam sat at a tap.
Tap, tap.
Sam sat.

slides.teacher_cue: Read the same passage again. This time, keep going without stopping. Smoother.
slides.expected_response: Students read more fluently on the second pass — fewer hesitations.
slides.correction_move: If still hesitant, re-model the tricky line, then have students re-read it once.

slides.teacher_cue: Listen and write. /s/ /a/ /t/. Write one sound in each box.
slides.expected_response: Students write s-a-t correctly in three boxes with accurate left-to-right encoding.
slides.correction_move: Re-segment orally: /s/ — write it. /a/ — write it. /t/ — write it. Check letter shapes.

slides.teacher_cue: Listen and write. /t/ /a/ /p/. Write one sound in each box.
slides.expected_response: Students write t-a-p correctly in three boxes.
slides.correction_move: Re-segment: /t/ — write it. /a/ — write it. /p/ — write it. Confirm each letter.

slides.teacher_cue: Listen and write. /a/ /t/. Two sounds — two boxes.
slides.expected_response: Students write a-t correctly. Short /a/ vowel is represented accurately.
slides.correction_move: Segment orally: /a/ then /t/. Write each. Check that A is written, not E or I.

content_payload.notes_field: Keep this light and oral. Say the word pair aloud. Ask: what changed? G1 does not need formal morpheme names.

slides.teacher_cue: Say: tap. Now say: taps. What did we add? (the /s/ sound). Oral only — no writing.
slides.expected_response: Students notice that something was added to the end of the word. They can say the added sound.
slides.correction_move: Say both words again slowly: tap — taps. Point to the added part. Say it together.

content_payload.comprehension_prompt: What did Sam do? Where was Sam?

slides.teacher_cue: Read the sentence. Then ask: What did Sam do? Where was Sam? Students answer in English.
slides.expected_response: Students answer: Sam sat. Sam was at a tap. Full sentence responses are ideal.
slides.correction_move: Re-read the sentence together. Point to 'sat' — what does that mean? Point to 'at a tap'.

check_items.label: Can write sat or tap from dictation

content_payload.notes_field: Mark each phoneme or skill target separately. Korean transfer flag available per item.

slides.teacher_cue: Quick final check. Mark each item: Secure, Shaky, or Missed. This feeds the lesson record.
slides.expected_response: Secure = accurate and automatic. Shaky = accurate with hesitation or prompting. Missed = unable to produce reliably.
slides.correction_move: Items marked Missed should be flagged for review at the start of next lesson.
